    <h1 class="devsite-page-title" tabindex="-1">
      Embeddings<devsite-actions hidden data-nosnippet>
    <devsite-llm-tools></devsite-llm-tools></devsite-actions>
  
      
    </h1>
  <div class="devsite-page-title-meta"><devsite-view-release-notes></devsite-view-release-notes></div>
  

  <devsite-toc class="devsite-nav"
    depth="2"
    devsite-toc-embedded
    >
  </devsite-toc>
  
    
  <div class="devsite-article-body clearfix
  ">

  
    
    
<p>
</p>

<p></p>































<p>The Gemini API offers embedding models to generate embeddings for text, images,
video, and other content. These resulting embeddings can then be used for tasks
such as semantic search, classification, and clustering, providing more accurate,
context-aware results than keyword-based approaches.</p>

<p>The latest model, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>, is the first multimodal
embedding model in the Gemini API. It maps text, images,
video, audio, and documents into a unified embedding space, enabling cross-modal
search, classification, and clustering across over 100 languages. See the
<a href="#multimodal">multimodal embeddings section</a> to learn more. For text-only
use cases, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code> remains available.</p>

<p>Building Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems is a common use case for
AI products. Embeddings play a key role in significantly enhancing model outputs
with improved factual accuracy, coherence, and contextual richness. If you prefer
to use a managed RAG solution, we built the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/file-search">File Search</a>
tool which makes doing RAG easier to manage and more cost effective.</p>

<h2 id="generate-embeddings" data-text="Generating embeddings" tabindex="-1">Generating embeddings</h2>

<p>Use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">embedContent</code> method to generate text embeddings:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">result</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">models</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embed_content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"gemini-embedding-2"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-n">contents</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"What is the meaning of life?"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nb">print</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">result</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embeddings</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="javascript" data-text="JavaScript" tabindex="-1">JavaScript</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JavaScript"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"@google/genai"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-k">async</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kd">function</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">main</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kd">const</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">ai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-ow">new</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">({});</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kd">const</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">response</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">await</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">ai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">models</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">embedContent</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">({</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'gemini-embedding-2'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">contents</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'What is the meaning of life?'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">});</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">console</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">log</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">response</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">embeddings</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">);</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">main</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">();</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="java" data-text="Java" tabindex="-1">Java</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Java"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">com.google.genai.Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">com.google.genai.types.EmbedContentResponse</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">java.util.Collections</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">new</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">();</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">EmbedContentResponse</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">response</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span>

</devsite-selector></div><aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> While <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code> lets you generate individual embeddings for a
list of strings, Gemini Embedding 2 produces a single aggregated embedding for
multiple inputs. You can find more information in <a href="#embedding-aggregation">Embedding aggregation</a>,
or you can use the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#batch-embedding">Batch API</a> if
you want to generate multiple embeddings at once.</span></aside>
<h2 id="task-types" data-text="Specify task type to improve performance" tabindex="-1">Specify task type to improve performance</h2>

<p>You can use embeddings for a wide range of tasks from classification to document
search. Specifying the right task type helps optimize the embeddings for the
intended relationships, maximizing accuracy and efficiency.</p>

<h3 id="task-types-embeddings-2" data-text="Task types with Embeddings 2" tabindex="-1">Task types with Embeddings 2</h3>

<p>For text-only tasks with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>, we strongly recommend you
add the task instruction in your prompt. This can be done by formatting the
query and the document with the correct task prefix.</p>

<p>When generating a <a href="#embedding-aggregation">single embedding based on multimodal
input</a>, we generally don&#39;t recommend prefixing the text
portion of the input with a task instruction. In some cases it improves
performance, but in others it reduces performance.</p>

<p>The following tables show examples of how to format queries and documents for
symmetric and asymmetric use cases using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> model.</p>

<p><strong>Retrieval use cases (Asymmetric format)</strong></p>

<p>In asymmetric use cases, add the task prefix to the query and apply
the document structure for the content you want to embed and retrieve.</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Use case</th>
<th>Query structure</th>
<th>Document structure</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Search query</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: search result | query: {content}</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">title: {title} | text: {content}</code><br>If there is no title, use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">title: none</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Question answering</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: question answering | query: {content}</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">title: {title} | text: {content}</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Fact checking</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: fact checking | query: {content}</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">title: {title} | text: {content}</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Code retrieval</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: code retrieval | query: {content}</code></td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">title: {title} | text: {content}</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p><strong>Example usage</strong></p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_1" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># Generate embedding for a task's query. Use your correct task here:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-k">def</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nf">prepare_query</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">query</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">):</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># return f"task: question answering | query: {query}"</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># return f"task: fact checking | query: {query}"</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># return f"task: code retrieval | query: {query}"</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-k">return</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-sa">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"task: search result | query: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">query</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># Generate embedding for document of an asymmetric retrieval task:</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-k">def</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nf">prepare_document</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">title</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-kc">None</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">):</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-k">if</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">title</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-ow">is</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-kc">None</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-n">title</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"none"</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-k">return</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-sa">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"title: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">title</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2"> | text: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<p><strong>Single-input use cases (Symmetric format)</strong></p>

<p>In symmetric use cases, for the same task, use the same formatting
for the query and the document.</p>

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Use case</th>
<th>Input structure</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Classification</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: classification | query: {content}</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Clustering</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: clustering | query: {content}</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Semantic similarity</td>
<td><code translate="no" dir="ltr">task: sentence similarity | query: {content}</code><br>Do not use this for search or retrieval. It is intended for semantic textual similarity.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<p><strong>Example usage</strong></p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_2" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># Generate embedding for query &amp; document of your task.</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-k">def</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nf">prepare_query_and_document</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">):</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># return f'task: clustering | query: {content}'</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># return f'task: sentence similarity | query: {content}'</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-k">return</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-sa">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'task: classification | query: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<p>It is important that the task is used consistently. E.g., if documents are
embedded with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">f&#39;task: classification | query: {content}&#39;</code>, the query should
also be embedded following this task format.</p>

<h3 id="task-types-embeddings-1" data-text="Task types with Embeddings 1" tabindex="-1">Task types with Embeddings 1</h3>

<p>For <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code>, you can specify the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">task_type</code> in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">embedContent</code>
method. For a complete list of supported task types, see the <a href="#supported-task-types">Supported task types</a>
table.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> You cannot use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">task_type</code> field for the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> model. Instead, include the task as an instruction in your prompt, as detailed in the <a href="#task-types-embeddings-2">above section</a>.</span></aside>
<p>The following example shows how you can use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY</code> to check how
similar in meaning strings of texts are.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_3" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">pandas</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">as</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">pd</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">sklearn.metrics.pairwise</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">cosine_similarity</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">texts</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"What is the meaning of life?"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"What is the purpose of existence?"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

<section><h3 id="rest_1" data-text="REST" tabindex="-1">REST</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">curl<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-embedding-001:embedContent"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-se">\</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span>-H<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"Content-Type: application/json"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-se">\</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span>-H<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"x-goog-api-key: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nv">$GEMINI_API_KEY</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-se">\</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span>-d<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">    "taskType": "SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY",</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">    "content": {</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        "parts": [</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        {</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">            "text": "What is the meaning of life?"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        },</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        {</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">            "text": "How much wood would a woodchuck chuck?"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        },</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        {</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">            "text": "How does the brain work?"</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        }</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">        ]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">    }</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-s1">    }'</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<p>The code snippets will show how similar the different chunks of text are to one
another when run.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Cosine similarity is a good distance metric because it focuses on
direction rather than magnitude, which more accurately reflects conceptual
closeness. Values range from -1 (opposite) to 1 (greatest similarity).</span></aside>
<h4 id="supported-task-types" data-text="Supported task types" tabindex="-1">Supported task types</h4>

<p>Supported task types for <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code>:</p>

<table>

 <th>Task type</th>
 <th>Description</th>
 <th>Examples</th>
 <tr>
   <td><b>SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY</b></td>
   <td>Embeddings optimized to assess text similarity.</td>
   <td>Recommendation systems, duplicate detection</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>CLASSIFICATION</b></td>
   <td>Embeddings optimized to classify texts according to preset labels.</td>
   <td>Sentiment analysis, spam detection</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>CLUSTERING</b></td>
   <td>Embeddings optimized to cluster texts based on their similarities.</td>
   <td>Document organization, market research, anomaly detection </td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</b></td>
   <td>Embeddings optimized for document search.</td>
   <td>Indexing articles, books, or web pages for search.</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>RETRIEVAL_QUERY</b></td>
   <td>
        Embeddings optimized for general search queries.
        Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_QUERY</code> for queries; <code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</code> for documents to be retrieved.
    </td>
   <td>Custom search</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY</b></td>
   <td>
    Embeddings optimized for retrieval of code blocks based on natural language queries.
    Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY</code> for queries; <code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</code> for code blocks to be retrieved.
   </td>
   <td>Code suggestions and search</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>QUESTION_ANSWERING</b></td>
   <td>
    Embeddings for questions in a question-answering system, optimized for finding documents that answer the question.
    Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">QUESTION_ANSWERING</code> for questions; <code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</code> for documents to be retrieved.
   </td>
   <td>Chatbox</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>FACT_VERIFICATION</b></td>
   <td>
    Embeddings for statements that need to be verified, optimized for retrieving documents that contain evidence supporting or refuting the statement.
    Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">FACT_VERIFICATION</code> for the target text; <code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</code> for documents to be retrieved
   </td>
   <td>Automated fact-checking systems</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="control-embedding-size" data-text="Controlling embedding size" tabindex="-1">Controlling embedding size</h2>

<p>Both <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> are trained using
the Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) technique which teaches a model to
learn high-dimensional embeddings that have initial segments (or prefixes) which
are also useful, simpler versions of the same data.</p>

<p>Use the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">output_dimensionality</code> parameter to control the size of
the output embedding vector. Selecting a smaller output dimensionality can save
storage space and increase computational efficiency for downstream applications,
while sacrificing little in terms of quality. By default, both models output a
3072-dimensional embedding, but you can truncate it to a smaller size without
losing quality to save storage space. We recommend using 768, 1536, or 3072
output dimensions.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_4" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">result</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">models</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embed_content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"gemini-embedding-2"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">contents</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"What is the meaning of life?"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>

<h2 id="quality-for-smaller-dimensions" data-text="Ensuring quality for smaller dimensions" tabindex="-1">Ensuring quality for smaller dimensions</h2>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> introduces automatic renormalization for non-default
dimensions.</span></aside>
<p>While the default 3072-dimension embeddings are always normalized, Gemini
Embedding 2 also auto-normalizes truncated dimensions (e.g., 768, 1536). This
ensures semantic similarity is calculated via vector direction rather than
magnitude, providing more accurate results out of the box.</p>

<p><strong>Older Models</strong>: If you are using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code>, you must manually
normalize non-3072 dimensions as follows:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_5" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">numpy</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-k">as</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">np</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">numpy.linalg</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">norm</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># Only for embeddings from `gemini-embedding-001`</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">embedding_values_np</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">np</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">array</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embedding_obj</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">values</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-n">normed_embedding</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">embedding_values_np</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">/</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">np</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">linalg</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">norm</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embedding_values_np</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nb">print</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-sa">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"Normed embedding length: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nb">len</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">normed_embedding</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-nb">print</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-sa">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"Norm of normed embedding: </span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">np</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">linalg</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">norm</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">normed_embedding</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">.6f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-si">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-c1"># Should be very close to 1</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
</devsite-selector></div>

Norm of normed embedding: 1.000000
</code></pre></devsite-code>

<h2 id="multimodal" data-text="Multimodal embeddings" tabindex="-1">Multimodal embeddings</h2>

<p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> model supports multimodal input, allowing you
to embed images, video, audio, and documents content alongside text. All modalities
are mapped into the same embedding space, enabling cross-modal search and
comparison.</p>

<h3 id="supported-modalities" data-text="Supported modalities and limits" tabindex="-1">Supported modalities and limits</h3>

<p>The overall maximum input tokens limit is 8192 tokens.</p>

<table>
 <th>Modality</th>
 <th>Specifications and limits</th>
 <tr>
   <td><b>Text</b></td>
   <td>Supports up to 8,192 tokens.</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>Image</b></td>
   <td>Maximum of 6 images per request. Supported formats: PNG, JPEG.
</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>Audio</b></td>
   <td>Maximum duration of 180 seconds. Supported formats: MP3, WAV.</td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
   <td><b>Video</b></td>
   <td>Maximum duration of 120 seconds. Supported formats: MP4, MOV. Supported codecs: H264, H265, AV1, VP9.<br>
   The system processes a maximum of 32 frames per video: short videos (≤32s) are sampled at 1 fps, while longer videos are uniformly sampled to 32 frames. Audio tracks are not processed in video files.
   </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
   <td><b>Documents (PDF)</b></td>
   <td>Maximum of 1 file per request, up to 6 pages.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h3 id="embed-images" data-text="Embedding images" tabindex="-1">Embedding images</h3>

<p>The following example shows how to embed an image using
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>.</p>

<p>Images can be provided as inline data or as uploaded files
through the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/files">Files API</a>.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_6" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-k">with</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-nb">open</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'example.png'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'rb'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-k">as</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">image_bytes</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">f</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">read</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">result</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">models</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embed_content</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'gemini-embedding-2'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">contents</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Part</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">from_bytes</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
            <span class="devsite-syntax-n">data</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">image_bytes</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
            <span class="devsite-syntax-n">mime_type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'image/png'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-p">),</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-p">]</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nb">print</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">result</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">embeddings</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="javascript_3" data-text="JavaScript" tabindex="-1">JavaScript</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JavaScript"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"@google/genai"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-w">        </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">contents</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">            </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">inlineData</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">                </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">mimeType</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'image/png'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">                </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">data</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">imgBase64</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

<h3 id="embedding-aggregation" data-text="Embedding aggregation" tabindex="-1">Embedding aggregation</h3>

<p>When working with multimodal content, how you structure your input affects the
embedding output:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Multiple parts (aggregated):</strong> Adding multiple inputs directly to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">contents</code> parameter produces one aggregated embedding for all inputs.</li>
<li><strong>Multiple <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Content</code> objects (separate):</strong> Wrapping each input in a
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Content</code> object and passing them in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">contents</code> parameter returns
separate embeddings for each entry.</li>
<li><strong>Post-level representation:</strong> For complex objects like social media posts
with multiple media items, we recommend aggregating separate embeddings
(for example, by averaging) to create a coherent post-level representation.</li>
</ul>

<p>The following example shows how to create one aggregated embedding for text and
image input. Simply add multiple inputs to the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">contents</code> parameter:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_7" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<h3 id="embed-video" data-text="Embedding video" tabindex="-1">Embedding video</h3>

<p>The following example shows how to embed a video using
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>.</p>

<p>Videos can be provided as inline data or as uploaded files
through the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/files">Files API</a>.</p>

    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'gemini-embedding-2'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

            <span class="devsite-syntax-n">mime_type</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'video/mp4'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

<p>If you need to embed videos &gt;120 seconds, you can chunk the video into
overlapping segments and embed those chunks individually.</p>

<h3 id="embed-documents" data-text="Embedding documents" tabindex="-1">Embedding documents</h3>

<p>Documents in PDF format can be embedded directly. The model processes the visual and text
content of each page.</p>

<p>PDFs can be provided as inline data or as uploaded files
through the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/files">Files API</a>.</p>

<h4 id="pdf-processing" data-text="How the model processes PDFs" tabindex="-1">How the model processes PDFs</h4>

<p>When you embed a PDF, the model processes the document using both visual and text features:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Visual representation:</strong> The model renders each page as an image, which consumes <strong>258 tokens</strong> per page.</li>
<li><strong>Text extraction:</strong> The model extracts text from the document. For <strong>native PDFs</strong> (which contain digital text), the model extracts the text directly. For <strong>scanned PDFs</strong> (which contain images of text), the model automatically runs optical character recognition (OCR) to extract the text.</li>
</ul>

<p>To calculate the total token count for a PDF, add the visual tokens (258 per page) to the text tokens. Your inputs must fit within the model&#39;s <strong>8,192 token limit</strong> (shared across all modalities). The system silently truncates inputs that exceed this limit.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The Gemini Developer API always enables OCR for PDFs and does not support disabling it (the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">document_ocr</code> parameter is only available in Vertex AI).</span></aside>
<h4 id="pdf-limits" data-text="PDF limits" tabindex="-1">PDF limits</h4>

<ul>
<li><strong>Files per request:</strong> You can submit a maximum of 1 PDF file.</li>
<li><strong>Page limit:</strong> You can submit a maximum of 6 pages per file. For the best quality, we strongly recommend using 1 page per PDF.</li>
</ul>

<p>The following example shows how to embed a PDF using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">

    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'gemini-embedding-2'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

<h2 id="common-use-cases" data-text="Use cases" tabindex="-1">Use cases</h2>

<p>Text embeddings are crucial for a variety of common AI use cases, such as:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG):</strong> Embeddings enhance the quality
of generated text by retrieving and incorporating relevant information into
the context of a model.</li>
<li><p><strong>Information retrieval:</strong> Search for the most semantically similar text or
documents given a piece of input text.</p>

<p><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/Talk_to_documents_with_embeddings.ipynb">
    Document search tutorial<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">task</span>
</a></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Search reranking</strong>: Prioritize the most relevant items by semantically
scoring initial results against the query.</p>

<p><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/Search_reranking_using_embeddings.ipynb">
    Search reranking tutorial<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">task</span>
</a></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Anomaly detection:</strong> Comparing groups of embeddings can help identify
hidden trends or outliers.</p>

<p><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/Anomaly_detection_with_embeddings.ipynb">
    Anomaly detection tutorial<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bubble_chart</span>
</a></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Classification:</strong> Automatically categorize text based on its content, such
as sentiment analysis or spam detection</p>

<p><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/Classify_text_with_embeddings.ipynb">
    Classification tutorial<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">token</span>
</a></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Clustering:</strong> Effectively grasp complex relationships by creating clusters
and visualizations of your embeddings.</p>

<p><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/clustering_with_embeddings.ipynb">
    Clustering visualization tutorial<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bubble_chart</span>
</a></p></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="store-embeddings" data-text="Storing embeddings" tabindex="-1">Storing embeddings</h2>

<p>As you take embeddings to production, it is common to
use <strong>vector databases</strong> to efficiently store, index, and retrieve
high-dimensional embeddings. Google Cloud offers managed data services that
can be used for this purpose including
<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/BUILD/vector-search-2">Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Vector Search 2.0</a>,
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction">BigQuery</a>,
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs/overview">AlloyDB</a>, and
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/introduction">Cloud SQL</a>.</p>

<p>The following tutorials show how to use other third party vector databases
with Gemini Embedding.</p>

<ul>
<li><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://docs.trychroma.com/integrations/embedding-models/google-gemini">
    ChromaDB tutorials<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bolt</span>
</a></li>
<li><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://qdrant.tech/documentation/embeddings/gemini/">
    QDrant tutorials<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bolt</span>
</a></li>
<li><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/model-providers/google">
    Weaviate tutorials<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bolt</span>
</a></li>
<li><a class="button button-with-icon" href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/examples/langchain/Gemini_LangChain_QA_Pinecone_WebLoad.ipynb">
    Pinecone tutorials<span class="material-icons icon-after" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">bolt</span>
</a></li>
</ul>

    <section>
      <h3 id="gemini-embedding" data-text="Gemini Embedding" tabindex="-1">Gemini Embedding</h3>
      <table class="gemini-api-model-table">
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">Property</th>
          <th scope="col">Description</th>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><span class="google-symbols" aria-hidden="true">id_card</span>Model code</td>
          <td class="gemini-api-model-table-grid">
            <section>
              <p><b>Gemini API</b></p>
              <p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code></p>
            </section>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><span class="google-symbols" aria-hidden="true">save</span>Supported data types</td>
          <td class="gemini-api-model-table-grid">
            <section>
              <p><b>Input</b></p>
              <p>Text</p>
            </section>
            <section>
              <p><b>Output</b></p>
              <p>Text embeddings</p>
            </section>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><span class="google-symbols" aria-hidden="true">token_auto</span>Token limits<sup><a href="/gemini-api/docs/tokens" rel="footnote">[*]</a></sup></td>
          <td class="gemini-api-model-table-grid">
            <section>
              <p><b>Input token limit</b></p>
              <p>2,048</p>
            </section>

              <p>Flexible, supports: 128 - 3072, Recommended: 768, 1536, 3072</p>
            </section>

</div>

<p>For deprecated Embeddings models, visit the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/deprecations">Deprecations</a> page</p>

<h2 id="migration" data-text="Migration from gemini-embedding-001" tabindex="-1">Migration from gemini-embedding-001</h2>

<p>The embedding spaces between <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code> and
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> are <strong>incompatible</strong>. This means you cannot
directly compare embeddings generated by one model with embeddings generated by
the other. If you are upgrading to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>, you must
re-embed all of your existing data.</p>

<p>Beyond incompatibility, there are several other notable differences between
the two models:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Task type specification:</strong> With <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code>, you specify the
task type using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">task_type</code> parameter (e.g., <code translate="no" dir="ltr">SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY</code>,
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT</code>). With <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code>, the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">task_type</code>
parameter is not supported. Instead, you should include task instructions
directly in the prompt for text-only tasks. See
<a href="#task-types-embeddings-2">Task types with Embeddings 2</a> for details on how
to format prompts for different use cases.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Embedding aggregation:</strong> <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code> generates individual
embeddings for each string in a list of inputs. In contrast,
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> produces a single, aggregated embedding when multiple
inputs (like text and images) are provided directly in one request. To
generate separate embeddings for individual inputs, wrap each input in a
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Content</code> object, or use the
<a href="/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#batch-embedding">Batch API</a>. See
<a href="#embedding-aggregation">Embedding aggregation</a> for more information.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Normalization:</strong> If you use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">output_dimensionality</code> to request embeddings
with fewer than 3072 dimensions, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-2</code> automatically
normalizes these truncated embeddings. With <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-embedding-001</code>, you
need to perform manual normalization for dimensions other than 3072. See
<a href="#quality-for-smaller-dimensions">Ensuring quality for smaller dimensions</a>
for details.</p></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="batch-embedding" data-text="Batch embeddings" tabindex="-1">Batch embeddings</h2>

<p>If latency is not a concern, try using the Gemini Embeddings models with
<a href="/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#batch-embedding">Batch API</a>. This
allows for much higher throughput at 50% of the default Embedding price.
Find examples on how to get started in the <a href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/quickstarts/Batch_mode.ipynb">Batch API cookbook</a>.</p>

<h2 id="responsible-use-notice" data-text="Responsible use notice" tabindex="-1">Responsible use notice</h2>

<p>Unlike generative AI models that create new content, the Gemini Embedding model
is only intended to transform the format of your input data into a numerical
representation. While Google is responsible for providing an embedding model
that transforms the format of your input data to the numerical-format requested,
users retain full responsibility for the data they input and the resulting
embeddings. By using the Gemini Embedding model you confirm that you have the
necessary rights to any content that you upload. Do not generate content that
infringes on others&#39; intellectual property or privacy rights. Your use of this
service is subject to our <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy">Prohibited Use
Policy</a> and
<a href="/gemini-api/terms">Google&#39;s Terms of Service</a>.</p>

<h2 id="start-building" data-text="Start building with embeddings" tabindex="-1">Start building with embeddings</h2>

<p>Check out the <a href="https://github.com/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/quickstarts/Embeddings.ipynb">embeddings quickstart
notebook</a>
to explore the model capabilities and learn how to customize and visualize your
embeddings.</p>
